sights.w: A small crescent-shaped coral island (0.47 km², highest point 26.9 m) off the Motobu Peninsula, nicknamed 'Croissant Island' because it looks like one from the air. The OCVB lists it and its Minna Beach as a day-trip swimming and snorkelling spot.
sights.k: The croissant-shaped coral island off Motobu

sights.n: Nyatiya Cave 'Sennin-gama', Ie Island (ニャティヤ洞)
sights.w: A seaside cave on Ie Island's south-west coast that sheltered so many islanders as an air-raid shelter in the Second World War that it is also called the 'Thousand-person cave'. Inside sits the 'chikara-ishi' power stone, said to bless with children whoever lifts it. Free to visit; listed by the Ie village office, the OCVB and Rurubu.

sights.n: Ōgimi Village Bashōfu Hall, Kijoka (大宜味村立芭蕉布会館)
sights.w: The village hall of Kijoka bashōfu, the banana-fibre cloth worn from Ryūkyū royalty to commoners; the Kijoka Bashōfu Preservation Society was designated an Important Intangible Cultural Property in 1974, and its leader Taira Toshiko (1921–2022) was a Living National Treasure. Visitors can watch the weaving process and buy bashōfu goods; entry is free.

sights.n: Kin Kannon-ji Temple, Kin (金武観音寺)
sights.w: A Kōyasan Shingon temple (mountain name Kinpusan, main image Shō-Kannon) traditionally founded in the 16th century by the monk Nisshū, who was shipwrecked at Kin while sailing from Kii and preached from the limestone cave beside the temple. Kin town's tourism site lists the cave (Nisshū-dō) and the temple's old fukugi trees.
sights.k: 16th-century temple over the Kin limestone cave

sights.n: Fukuji Dam & Lake Fukujō, Higashi (福地ダム・福上湖)
sights.address: Fukuji River, Higashi-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: Completed in 1974 on the Fukuji River, Okinawa's largest dam holds the prefecture's biggest reservoir, Lake Fukujō, chosen in 2005 as one of Japan's 100 best dam lakes. The Yanbaru three-villages tourism portal lists its lookouts, lakeside paths and water-resources exhibit hall, with nature-watching boat and canoe trips on the lake.
sights.k: Okinawa's largest dam lake in the Yanbaru forest
